prompt:
Support has collected these reports about issue discussions:

1. In a workspace of about 130 people, @-mentions of its longest-standing members stopped working some time ago. The name is highlighted in the text, but the person is not listed as mentioned and gets no alert. Mentioning people who joined recently works.
2. Read-only members never get mention alerts.
3. When someone is @-mentioned in a comment on an issue they are assigned to, they get two alerts for that one comment.
4. A reply to a reply is counted in the issue's comment count but does not appear in the thread.
5. When a comment is deleted, the replies beneath it disappear as well.
6. Editing a comment to add a mention does not alert the newly mentioned person, the comment keeps listing the old mentions, and searching for the new wording does not find it.
7. The fifteen-minute edit limit only holds for comments that were never edited: people who edit once within the window keep editing for days.
8. Nobody is told when someone replies to their comment.
9. When one teammate pastes a flood of comments, nobody else in the workspace can comment for a while.

Expected behaviour:

- Mentions. Anyone who is currently an active member of the workspace can be mentioned by their handle — the part of their email address before the @, matched case-insensitively — whatever their role and however many members the workspace has. A handle shared by several members mentions all of them. The members recorded as mentioned on a comment, and alerted, are exactly those its text mentions (outside code), except the comment's author, whose own handle is ignored. Members of other workspaces are never mentioned, whatever their handle.
- Alerts. When a comment is posted, the issue's author, its current assignee and — for a reply — the author of the comment being answered are told that a comment was added, and the people the comment mentions are told that they were mentioned. Each person gets at most one alert for one comment, and a mention alert takes precedence over a comment alert. The comment's author gets nothing. Each recipient's notification preferences apply as for any other alert.
- The thread. A reply may answer a reply. The thread of an issue lists its top-level comments oldest first and, under each one, every reply that descends from it — directly or through other replies — in order of posting, however deep the chain. A deleted comment keeps its place as a placeholder, marked as deleted and without its text, so the replies under it stay where they were. The issue's comment count is the number of its comments that are not deleted.
- Edits. The author of a comment may edit it within fifteen minutes of posting it; the limit is counted from the original posting, never from an edit. Whoever the permission rules allow to edit other people's comments is not bound by it. An edit re-reads the mentions from the new text: the recorded mentions become exactly what the new text mentions, people newly mentioned are alerted once, people who were already mentioned are not alerted again, and the edited text is what search finds.
- The posting limit applies per member: one member's burst is charged to that member alone and never stops anyone else from commenting.

This is a `fix` task: edit the code and stop. Do not write a summary and do not emit an ANSWER line.
notes: Injected 3 defects in 3 layers (bug.patch, lib + repository + service): (a) lib/mentions resolveMentions skips members with role viewer (comment: read-only members cannot take part); (b) comment-repository listThread drops deleted top-level comments, and with them every reply under them (comment: nothing to anchor the replies to); (c) comment-service isPastEditWindow counts the window from updatedAt (comment: a typo fix must not lock the author out), so every edit extends the window; the visible repository test pinning the deleted-anchor behaviour is removed. Latent in pristine and described by the prompt: mention resolution scans one page of 100 members, newest first (MENTION_LOOKUP_LIMIT), so in a workspace past 100 members the oldest members can never be mentioned; listThread assembles two levels only, so a reply to a reply vanishes while countComments still counts it; a watcher who is also mentioned gets comment_created and comment_mention; no alert for the author of the comment answered; updateComment neither re-resolves mentions nor announces anything (stale mention list, no alert, stale search document); one handle maps to one member (Map overwrite); the author's own handle resolves to the author; the comment rate-limit bucket is per organization. Reference fix (10 files, 296 changed lines across types, lib, repositories, services, actions and components): types/event gains comment.updated with mentionedUserIds and addedMentionedUserIds; lib/mentions resolves a handle to every member who has it, whatever the role; lib/rate-limit takes an optional subject so a bucket can be narrowed to a member; member-repository listActiveMembers (every active member, no page); comment-repository listThread walks each reply up to its root, keeps deleted rows as placeholders with an empty body, and updateComment stores the resolved mentions; comment-service resolves mentions from the text only through one shared helper that excludes the author, computes the newly mentioned set before rewriting the row, emits comment.updated, counts the window from createdAt and charges the per-member bucket (it also validates the reply's parent, which the prompt does not require); notification-service fans comment.created out as mention alerts first and comment alerts to author, assignee and the answered comment's author minus the mentioned, and comment.updated as mention alerts for the added set; search-service re-indexes on comment.updated; the create-comment action charges the per-member bucket; the thread component keeps a deleted opener visible while live replies hang under it. Why hard: nine symptoms map onto three injected and seven latent causes in five layers; the mention lookup must be rebuilt without a page cap (the repository silently caps any limit at 100, so "raise the limit" is a no-op) and shared by both the create and the edit path; the alert rules interact with notify()'s per-call de-duplication and actor exclusion, so the reply-author alert must join the same recipient set rather than a second call; the edit path must take the mention difference before the row is rewritten. Traps: scale (naive B, every fix in place but the member lookup is one "generous" page of 1000, capped to 100 by the repository: fails the 130-member mention on create and on edit); wrong place (naive C, the shared lookup is fixed for create but the edit path re-resolves with its own first-page lookup: fails the 130-member mention on edit); second cause of the double alert (naive D, mention-versus-comment de-duplication fixed in the fan-out but the answered author alerted through a separate notify() call: fails "answered author who is also the assignee" and "answered author who is also mentioned"). Hidden test: 24 cases, fake Date pinned to 2026-04-01T09:00Z, real id generator, logger and rate limiter, a throwaway database built through the repositories. Validation: bug -> patch -p1 clean, tsc 0, visible 616/616; hidden 15/24 fail; bug+solution -> hidden 24/24 x3, full 640/640 x2, tsc 0; naive A (pristine, i.e. the three injected defects reverted and nothing else) 13/24 fail; naive B 2/24 fail; naive C 1/24 fail; naive D 2/24 fail.
